main_text.p: sumpta, deprehendatur eam auth. socorditer translatam & compilatam esse: vid. Duaren. tit. de judic. c. de Var. Judic. Præcept. Conn. 1. Comm. 11.
main_text.head: SECTIO QUARTA.
CAPUT PRIMUM.
main_text.p: 1. SEquitur jus particulare, seu non commune, quod uno vocabulo usitatissimo, Statutum, dicitur, quasi statum publicum tuens, secundum Andream ab Exea in c. canonum Statuta. de Constit. tom. 2. Repet. jur. can. p. 182. n. 46. Appellatur etiam jus municipale; ut hic tamen paulo latius sir acceptum. Forte apud Cæsarem in init. Belli Gallici, Instituti nomine designatum. Etiam in jure nostro dicta lex, seu lex municipii, quemadmodum in genere

page.notes: The initial S is a large woodcut letter joined to "Equitur". The first word of the body is printed as "SEquitur" with the initial. Some ink spots are present on the page and were ignored. The opening word "sumpta" begins a fragment carried over from the previous page. Possible misreading in "sir acceptum", which may read "sit". Page number 123 is printed at top right.
